title: The finite first-degree image-sum filtration is a subcomplex
statement: Let C be abelian [def-sp-abelian] and K a Z×Z bicomplex with a total complex [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Define its first finite image-sum filtration [def-sp-filtration] in degree n by the supremum over r≤p≤n of the images of the inclusions K^{p,n-p}→Tot(K)^n. For every r,n the total differential Tot(K)^n→Tot(K)^{n+1} restricts to a morphism between these r-th steps. No quadrant hypothesis is required.

source.place: Section Spectral sequences: double complexes, section-double-complex, paragraph defining F_I and F_II before lemma-ss-double-complex

proof.text: On the summand (p,n-p), the total differential is the signed sum of the horizontal component into (p+1,n-p) and the vertical component into (p,n-p+1). If r≤p≤n, both target first degrees lie in [r,n+1]. Each component factors through the corresponding target image and thus the target finite supremum. Scalar signs and addition preserve factorization through a subobject. Pull back this target subobject along the total differential. Each source diagonal inclusion factors through the pullback, so its image lies in the pullback. Their finite supremum lies there by Finset.sup_le. The pullback factorization gives the required restriction and its commuting equation.

lean.statement: theorem firstFiltration_differential {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (K : HomologicalComplex₂ C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) [K.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] (r n : ℤ) : ∃ f : ((K.firstFiltration n).step r : C) ⟶ ((K.firstFiltration (n + 1)).step r : C), f ≫ ((K.firstFiltration (n + 1)).step r).arrow = ((K.firstFiltration n).step r).arrow ≫ (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).d n (n + 1)
